description_full: YPF Sociedad Anónima, an energy company, engages in the oil and gas upstream and downstream activities in South America and Argentina. The company operates through the Upstream, Midstream and Downstream, LNG and Integrated Gas, and New Energies segments. It is involved in the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of crude oil and natural gas; the refining, transportation and commercialization of refined products; the production, transportation, and commercialization of petrochemical products; the transportation and commercialization of crude oil; and the commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry, and of grains and their by-products. The company also offers fertilizers and crop protection products; flours, oils, and grains; asphalts; naphtha; and petroleum coke. In addition, it engages in the natural gas transportation and commercialization to third parties and to the Midstream and Downstream segments; the separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, and storage and transportation to produce ethane, propane, butane, and gasoline, as well as its commercialization; the development of liquefied natural gas liquefaction capacity; and power generation activities. The company was incorporated in 1977 and is based in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

financial_summary: YPF Sociedad Anonima is a large-cap energy business with a $14.9B market cap on $13.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 2% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 16% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $1.7B in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 11.0× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
